one_month_reasoning: Inside the window: Q3 2026 results, most likely Thu Oct 22 (not yet announced; FCX reported Q3 on Oct 19-23 every year and 2026 quarters on Thursdays; Oct 15 is a vendor placeholder). Consensus Q3 EPS $0.74 on guided 750 Mlb Cu at a $6.00 H2 deck while realized copper ran ~$6.3-6.7, so a price-driven beat is expected and largely priced; the swing factor is the Grasberg ramp language (80% by mid-2027) and the first 2027 volume/cost/capex framing. Section 232 refined-copper tariff: undecided after the notional window lapsed Sep 28; Reuters reported it stalled before the midterms, and the front-month COMEX premium has already gone (SMM Sep 29), so a 'no tariff' headline would do less near-term damage than I assumed in round 1. Momentum (+98% year) and reversal after a record-copper month roughly offset. I stay near-symmetric: median ~$70.4, monthly log-sigma 14% (48%/3.5 plus a small earnings premium). Unchanged from round 1 in substance.

fair_value.method: Blend of attributable P/E (2028E EPS $4.00 at a $5.75/lb deck x 16x = $64, weight 0.45), FCF yield (2027E attributable FCF $3.10/sh at 4.75% = $65, weight 0.30) and a rebuilt EV/EBITDA (2028E consolidated EBITDA $16.5B x 8.5x, less $5.3B net debt, x 62% attributable = $58, weight 0.25) -> ~$63. At the supervisor's $6.00 deck the same framework gives ~$69; the gap is my base-rate-driven copper mean reversion.

base.story: Copper eases to ~$5.75-6.25, Grasberg reaches ~80% by mid-2027 and approaches full by year-end, and 2027 volume growth of >20% offsets price; the market pays ~16-17x a ~$4.0-4.2 2028 EPS. That is roughly flat to slightly down, in line with the conditional base-rate median (-2%).

bull.story: The supply deficit persists (Grasberg/Kamoa/Escondida disruptions, tariffs restarting US hoarding), copper holds $6.5-7.5, and management's model gives ~$18.5-20B EBITDA; EPS ~$5+ at 18-20x.

thesis_break_reason: Around $46 (-35%) the stock would be pricing copper back near $5/lb (~$13B 2027 EBITDA, EPS ~$3.1 at ~15x) or a second structural Grasberg setback or adverse IUPK terms. That is beyond ordinary copper-beta noise at 48% vol and would mean the volume-ramp-plus-tight-market thesis failed.

reasoning: Base rates (rerun from 2005-2026 FCX monthly closes, n=236): unconditional 12m forward median about +3%, log-sd 0.54, 10th/90th percentiles -44%/+84%. Conditional on a trailing +40% year and price within 15% of the 12m high (n=54, overlapping), the median is -2% with a 50% hit rate and log-sd 0.51. The +60% bucket (+12% median) is dominated by early-recovery rallies, and today's 24-month return (+41%) does not match those rebounds. The supervisor was right that my four copper-record analogues are a weak n=4 prior with no Grasberg-like 20%+ volume ramp. I downgrade them from an anchor to a tilt, which moves my median from $66 up to $68, close to the conditional base-rate median. Valuation: my round-1 $2.80 EPS was a Q2 run-rate error. Rebuilt with guided ≥3.72 Blb, management's EBITDA sensitivity, 32% tax and 38% NCI, EPS is $3.70 (2027) / $4.00 (2028) at a $5.75 deck, vs $4.16 consensus at ~$6. The EV leg now deducts NCI at ~38% of equity (~$51B, not 18% of EV). Blended fair value is $63 (from $62). It barely moved because the corrections offset: higher EPS and a normal 16x in place of 22x on depressed EPS, and a much larger NCI deduction. I keep a $5.75 deck below the supervisor's $6.00 as my base-rate judgment (copper has not held record levels for 12 months in prior cycles), and I say so explicitly; each $0.25/lb is ~$5/share. I dropped the discounted inputs (the Substack 'FCX prices $5.90' claim, DB $22,050/t, Kalshi recession odds). Prediction markets add little: Polymarket's only copper market (copper cable in Section 232 by Dec 31, 2026) is 27% on $15.9K volume, too thin to move a number. Distribution: median $68 (-4%), a mixture of lognormals with sigma 0.42/0.56 (fat tails, 48% realized vol), which gives P(≥71) ≈ 0.46. Research in round 2 was limited to 3 queries plus the recomputation.
